description:
Liping Queshe is a green tea from Liping county in southeast Guizhou. Its name means sparrow's tongue, which describes the shape of the leaf rather than a separate tea plant, and many Chinese teas share this image, so the place in the name matters.

It belongs to the flat pan-fired greens. Beyond that the making is little documented.

Tasting notes for this tea alone are scarce. General descriptions of Liping tea mention sweetness and a strong aroma, so that is a fair starting expectation, not a verdict. Brew it as you would other small flat greens, with water around 80°C.

When buying, ask for the harvest date and look for even, unbroken leaf, as with any flat green.
